organic.name: Neem Oil Spray
organic.preparation: Mix 2 tablespoons of neem oil with 1 gallon of water and 1 teaspoon of mild soap
organic.application: Spray on affected parts, repeat every 7-10 days
organic.benefits: Biodegradable, safe for beneficial insects, multiple applications

organic.name: Copper-Based Fungicide
organic.preparation: Mix copper fungicide according to package instructions
organic.application: Spray foliage thoroughly, apply every 7-14 days
organic.benefits: Effective against wide range of fungal diseases
organic.availability: Available in most agricultural supply stores

organic.name: Compost Tea
organic.preparation: Steep compost in water for 24-48 hours, aerate regularly
organic.application: Soil drench or foliar spray, apply weekly
organic.benefits: Improves soil health, boosts plant immunity, provides nutrients

organic.name: Garlic-Chili Spray
organic.preparation: Blend 10 garlic cloves and 5 chilies with 1 liter water, strain
organic.application: Spray on affected plants, repeat every 5-7 days

chemical.name: Chlorothalonil
chemical.precautions: Wear protective clothing, avoid application during flowering

chemical.name: Imidacloprid
chemical.precautions: Toxic to bees, avoid application during flowering

chemical.name: Carbendazim
chemical.precautions: Avoid prolonged exposure, use protective gear

biological.name: Trichoderma viride
biological.dosage: 1-2 kg per hectare or 10g per kg seed

biological.name: Beauveria bassiana
biological.benefits: Fungal pathogen for insects, environmentally safe

biological.name: Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt)
biological.benefits: Specific to caterpillars, safe for humans and beneficial insects

general: Use disease-resistant and locally adapted varieties
Practice crop rotation (2-3 year rotation for most crops)
Maintain proper plant spacing for good air circulation
Avoid overhead watering to reduce leaf wetness
Remove and destroy infected plant debris
Keep fields free of weeds that can host pests and diseases
Monitor crops regularly for early detection
Apply balanced fertilizers based on soil tests
soil_management: Test soil annually and amend based on results
Maintain soil pH between 6.0-7.0 for most crops
Use cover crops to improve soil health
Avoid soil compaction through proper tillage
water_management: Water early in the day to allow leaves to dry
Use drip irrigation to reduce leaf wetness
Avoid overwatering which can lead to root diseases
Ensure proper drainage to prevent waterlogging
Mulch around plants to conserve moisture
integrated_pest_management: Encourage beneficial insects (lady beetles, lacewings, bees)
Apply pheromone traps for monitoring and control
Use biological control agents when available
Apply chemical controls only when necessary and as last resort

seasonal_tips.summer: Focus on irrigation management, monitor for heat stress
seasonal_tips.monsoon: Prevent fungal diseases, ensure proper drainage
seasonal_tips.winter: Protect from frost, adjust fertilizer application
seasonal_tips.spring: Optimal planting time for most vegetables

local_solutions: Plant windbreaks to reduce wind damage
Use shade nets for heat-sensitive crops

seasonal_tips.monsoon: Disease pressure highest, use resistant varieties

local_solutions: Use raised beds for better drainage
